_comment: Regional language variants a dialect technique translates the prompt into, on the machine-translation model (TranslateGemma), one row per technique (the dialect generator of combination_spec.json makes to_dialect_{slug}). It reuses the translation machinery (jailbreak/obfuscation/translation.py) under the translation switch. name: the variant as the prompt and info write it. slug: the end of the technique name. code: the region/script code TranslateGemma is sent (its chat template maps a region code to the base language's name and puts the code in the instruction). base: the base translation language of languages.json whose measured MEDIAN_RATIO the length band uses, since no dialect ratio is measured yet (a pod measurement is pending; Portuguese, not a translation language, has none either and uses 1.0). script: the ISO 15924 code of the variant's script. labels: the GlotLID labels the output may carry. GlotLID tells the base language, not the region. Mexican Spanish, Canadian French and Traditional Chinese take exactly their base language's labels as translation accepts them (translation.ACCEPTED_LABELS). Egyptian Arabic does not: it takes six of Arabic's nine (Egyptian arz, Standard arb, and apc, ajp, acm, ary), leaving out acq, aeb and ars; no measurement chose them. German (Switzerland) takes German's deu_Latn and also gsw_Latn: GlotLID may read Swiss Standard German (Swiss words, ss for the sharp s) as Swiss German, so refusing gsw would reject good pieces; the cost is that a Schweizerdeutsch output passes the label check too, and nothing else tells the two apart. Brazilian Portuguese has no base set (Portuguese is not a translation language): por_Latn and Galician glg_Latn. trad_share: for zh-Hant, the minimum share of Traditional characters among the marker characters of the piece: the 28 common characters whose Simplified and Traditional forms differ, in either form (dialect._SIMPLIFIED and _TRADITIONAL), not among all its Han characters; a piece with no marker character passes, since it cannot be told apart; omitted for the others. no_eszett: for de-CH (German (Switzerland): standard German as written in Switzerland, not the spoken Swiss German dialects, which no row covers), true: Swiss Standard German writes ss (SS) for the sharp s, so a piece holding the letter (lower or upper case) is rejected, reason eszett, and translated again; omitted for the others. Read from the package only.
